name: acyl-CoA dehydrogenase short chain

function.text: ACADS is the approved symbol for acyl-CoA dehydrogenase short chain. Reviewed functional annotations implicate its product in acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity; flavin adenine dinucleotide binding; butyrate catabolic process.

germline.text: Retained strong or definitive GenCC associations include short chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (autosomal recessive). Allele and inheritance require review.

somatic.text: Cancer Hotspots v1 reports recurrent residue-level observations in Colorectal carcinoma; Glioblastoma; Clear cell renal cell carcinoma. This is statistical recurrence evidence; it does not establish that every variant in this gene is a driver or a clinically actionable alteration. Evidence in this collection is restricted to the historical V1 release.

function.text: ACADS encodes acyl-CoA dehydrogenase short chain. Based in part on similarity, short-chain specific acyl-CoA dehydrogenase is one of the acyl-CoA dehydrogenases that catalyze the first step of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, an aerobic process breaking down fatty acids into acetyl-CoA and allowing the production of energy from fats. The first step of fatty acid beta-oxidation consists in the removal of one hydrogen from C-2 and C-3 of the straight-chain fatty acyl-CoA thioester, resulting in the formation of trans-2-enoyl-CoA.

germline.text: Germline disease associations include short chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (autosomal recessive).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving ACADS have been reported in glioblastoma, low-grade glioma, and colorectal carcinoma.
